title: Error Suppression in Distributed Quantum Computing with Heterogeneous-Distance Lattice Surgery
authors: Daniel Dilley, Anastashia Jebraeilli, Rayat Roy, Shobhit Gupta, Alvin Gonzales, Zain Saleem
abstract: Distributed quantum computing requires fault-tolerant operations across inter-QPU links that can be substantially noisier than local gates. Uniformly increasing code distance provides additional protection but also enlarges data patches used for local storage and computation. Here, we introduce distributed heterogeneous-distance lattice surgery using an eight-data-patch ancilla-mediated (8-DAM) architecture, which will be useful for near-term quantum devices with less qubit overhead. In this architecture, the central ancilla spanning the inter-QPU boundary is enlarged while the data patches retain distance $d$. The protocol uses traveling stabilizers to suppress hook errors during merge and split operations between these unequal-distance patches. Circuit-level simulations of rotated surface codes at fixed local depolarizing noise show that logical-readout error rates depend only weakly on link noise. The resulting advantage over conventional lattice surgery grows as link errors increase. Comparisons with uniform distance implementations demonstrate comparable logical error suppression with reduced physical-qubit overhead. We also demonstrate how 8-DAM layouts support two simultaneous distributed logical CNOT operations between four logical data qubits using a single enlarged ancilla. At higher link noise, this construction yields lower logical error rates and more stability than two independent distributed logical CNOTs. These results support selective ancilla enlargement as a resource-efficient approach to fault-tolerant distributed quantum computing.
summary: This paper proposes a resource-efficient method called heterogeneous-distance lattice surgery for fault-tolerant quantum computing across noisy links. By selectively enlarging the ancilla at the inter-QPU boundary while keeping data patches smaller, the authors significantly reduce physical qubit overhead compared to standard methods. Simulations show this approach maintains excellent error suppression even as link noise increases.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving fault-tolerant quantum operations across inter-QPU links, which are significantly noisier than local gates in distributed quantum computing architectures.
main_result: The proposed heterogeneous-distance lattice surgery (8-DAM) architecture maintains low logical error rates at high link noise while significantly reducing the physical qubit overhead compared to uniform-distance implementations.
method: The authors introduce a novel lattice surgery protocol using an enlarged central ancilla and traveling stabilizers to suppress hook errors during merge/split operations between unequal-distance data patches.
model_or_system: The model uses the rotated surface code implemented across modular Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) connected by noisy inter-QPU links. The core technique is the 8-DAM architecture, where the central ancilla is enlarged while data patches retain a smaller, fixed distance $d$.
key_observables: Logical-readout error rates, physical qubit overhead (qubit count), and the comparison of error suppression factors against uniform-distance lattice surgery.
important_parameters: Local depolarizing noise ($	ext{p}_{	ext{local}}$), inter-QPU link noise ($	ext{p}_{	ext{link}}$), and the specific distance parameters used in the heterogeneous construction (e.g., $3	ext{--}7	ext{--}3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that local QPU operations are fault-tolerant if the distance is high enough, and it specifically excludes modeling link-generation failures, leakage, or correlated link noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of the rotated surface code patches, the merge configurations for lattice surgery, and the resulting 8-DAM patch architecture, along with error rate comparisons for single and dual logical CNOT operations.
paper_structure: The paper reviews background on rotated surface codes and lattice surgery, presents the heterogeneous 8-DAM constructions and simulation results, and concludes by discussing the resource-efficient implications for fault-tolerant distributed quantum computing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the scaling bottleneck in quantum computing by providing a resource-efficient error correction scheme for noisy, modular interconnects, which is crucial for realizing large-scale quantum processors.
